_comment: Per-consumer governance (captain decision D4, 2026-08-26): one entry per
LiteLLM virtual key. provision_keys.py (helm hook + 15m CronJob in
helmrelease.yaml) reads this file and mints/updates a virtual key via the
/key API - LiteLLM has no config-file-only way to declare a budgeted key,
see docs/ai-system/litellm/README.md#why-postgres. Plain JSON (not YAML):
the provisioning Job is stdlib-only Python with no PyYAML dependency.
To add a consumer: add an entry to `consumers` below, add a matching
`data.match` block to pushsecret.yaml (secretKey == this entry's `name`),
commit. The provision-keys-sync CronJob (every 15m) re-reads this file
and is idempotent: an existing key keeps its value, only its
budget/rate-limit/model-list are re-synced. A Helm install/upgrade hook
also runs the same script immediately on first deploy.
To raise a budget later: edit the numbers below and commit. The existing
key is preserved (see previous line); only its limits change.
A key whose `models` list contains only the router alias `auto` can still
be routed to every tier backend AND still runs the classifier: verified
2026-08-26, the allow-list is checked against the model the CALLER asked
for, not the one the router resolves to. That makes `auto` a real
governance boundary - such a key cannot call claude-opus-5 directly, only
reach it by being classified into that tier.

consumers.name: demo
consumers._comment: D4: 'create a tiny budget first we will expand later.' Small enough to exhaust in one manual smoke test.

consumers.name: router-demo
_comment: D3 auto-router consumer. Scoped to the routed alias ONLY, which is the
point: this key reaches Anthropic exclusively through a classification
it does not control. Budget is deliberately small but larger than the
`demo` cap, because a routed request costs a classifier call plus the
completion. Measured 2026-08-26 on the lab rig: ~$0.0034 per
classification in governance accounting (the ~850-token rubric prefix
is prompt-cached by llama.cpp and cached tokens price at $0), plus the
tier backend's own cost - real USD once a request lands on a cloud
tier. Raise maxBudget here, not the tier prices, when this runs out.
